sections.title: The letter u
paragraphs: The letter (u) /u/ is named (u) /u/. Its main sound is heard in the word (uno) /ˈu.no/, which means one. This letter makes two spoken sounds in Spanish, and it can also stay completely silent.

sections.title: How to say u
paragraphs: For the main vowel, pull your tongue back and raise it high. Push your lips forward into a tight circle and vibrate your voice. For the quick gliding sound, make the same mouth shape, but glide right into the next vowel without stopping. Check your throat with your fingers to feel the continuous vibration.

sections.title: Spelling rules for u
paragraphs: As an ordinary vowel, the letter sounds like /u/, as in (luna) /ˈlu.na/. Next to another vowel, it turns into a quick glide like the sound /w/, as in (agua) /ˈa.ɣwa/. After the letters q or g before e or i, the letter is not pronounced at all. You can hear this silence in (guitarra) /ɡiˈta.ra/.

sections.title: Common mistakes with u
paragraphs: Do not let this vowel glide into two parts like the vowel sound in boot. Keep your tongue steady until the sound ends. Also, do not relax your mouth into the weak vowel heard in the word put. Make a tight circle with your lips every time.
